title: Her rooms on D deck (the saloon deck): R3, a sourced table of facts
written: 2026-11-20, by the R3 session (Claude Opus 5.5), under docs/research/RESEARCH_rooms_plans_licence_v1_1_2026-11-20.md, on the coordinator's word after F and G
rules: Facts only: which room, where, how big, which door to which. No image or drawing of any plan is kept. Every row cites the reference read and the original checked, or says it was not checked. Bets are tagged as bets.
reference: ET: Encyclopedia Titanica's free deck plans, D deck (https://www.encyclopedia-titanica.org/titanic-deckplans/d-deck.html; drawn by Bruce Beveridge for Titanic The Ship Magnificent, The History Press 2008), read on the page in the built-in browser on 2026-11-20, nothing saved
original: Shipbuilder 1911: The Shipbuilder, Midsummer 1911 (the Olympic and Titanic number), plate 4c, 'Saloon Deck D', as reproduced by GG Archives (https://www.ggarchives.com/OT/Titanic/25-ImageLibrary/TheShipbuilder-10-Design-SpecialPlates.html); too small to read room by room, not opened this time.
how: Walls by her frames, read off the frame numbers the reference prints along the centreline. D deck was read coarser than E, F and G: the browser pane was hidden, its screenshots came back at changing scales, so frames were read from the printed labels beside each wall (to about two frames) and the long walls were measured with the ruler in the page (to a pixel). Every row is tagged 'approx'.

Frames to feet: her frames are the same on every deck, so this table takes E deck's anchors (data/rooms/E_deck.json, measured there at the reference's scale), and its own 'stern' (D deck reaches about 8 ft further aft than E, on the counter) [approx].

y: feet from the centreline, port positive, at 0.0979 ft a pixel (the breadth over the shell amidships on this image: 947 px for 92.67 ft). 'shell+' and 'shell-' are her side; in metres the tool puts it at the model's half-breadth halfway between D and C decks [stand-in for the reference's shell].

No watertight bulkhead passes through D deck (A, B and K to P stop under it; C to J under E), and the reference draws none on it: the table's 'bulkheads' is empty, and its rows are not compared with the model's zones by compartment.
Doors: 2 ft 3 in by default [bet], unless the reference writes one.
Derived fields (x_m, y_m, poly_m, area_m2, zone, slab, plan_compartment) are written by: node tools/rooms_table.js --write data/rooms/D_deck.json

frames.note: E deck's anchors (her frames, feet forward of amidships), with D deck's own stern.

bulkheads.note: None: no watertight bulkhead passes through D deck, and the reference marks none on it.

side.note: Read 2026-11-20 between 22:50 and 23:02 CST, both sides, with the line test. D deck runs over the counter: its plan reaches about 152A. For BACKLOG G14 (the hull's ends): tools/rooms_table_tests.js sets each against the model's half-breadth. Frames 75A to 40A and 40F to 75F added 2026-11-21 between 05:20 and 05:45 CST by the B1+B2 lane, the same method in the built-in browser (nothing saved), for C3 (the epoch's hull ends, D80; G20's G14 half): every 5 frames, no reading off the smooth line through its neighbours by more than 0.1 m, so no single frames were added. At R3's 80A and 80F on C and D decks, and at 80F and 80A on E, the same reading gives R3's figures within 0.1 ft (one pixel).
side.unit: ft from the centreline to her outer line as the plan draws it, port and starboard, read on the page at 1:1 by pixel profile: from her outside inward, the first dark pixel that lies on a continuous line (a dark path running at least 28 px each way along her), at three columns 6 px apart about the frame's tick; the median of the three. Annotations outside her (labels, dimension arrows) fail the line test. null: no reading (the line broken there by fittings).
